title: ephemeral-snapshot-rotator-and-mini-replay-cli
author: Keiko Tanaka
release_notes: Adds an ephemeral snapshot rotator for compact oncall snapshots and a lightweight 'minireplay' CLI to replay snapshots for fast local repro and runbook validation.
description: Motivation: On-call responders frequently need small, focused snapshots they can replay locally to reproduce noisy incidents or validate playbook changes. Full snapshot exports are large and slow to transfer; long-lived snapshot stores increase telemetry retention costs. This PR introduces an ephemeral snapshot rotator plus a compact replay CLI that together provide a fast path for constructing, rotating, and locally replaying compact incident snapshots without changing the existing export format. Design and scope: 1) snapshot/rotator.go: an in-memory rolling buffer that keeps N most-recent compact snapshots per-service (configurable by count and byte budget). The rotator exposes a TTL-based eviction and a safe rotate API to atomically publish a compact snapshot for replay. 2) snapshot/reader.go: small helper to build a compact replay bundle (metadata, trimmed traces, top-k logs, condensed metrics timeseries) from live telemetry. 3) cmd/minireplay: a single-binary CLI that can fetch a snapshot from a rotator endpoint or read a local bundle and then replay it against local playbook runners or the incident-bot sandbox. CLI supports flags --max-events, --trim-level, --sandbox and outputs a concise replay summary and suggested next-playbook-steps. 4) telemetry/metrics: new metrics to instrument rotator churn, average bundle size, and replay success/failure rates so oncall SLOs can be monitored. 5) tests: integration test that spins up an ephemeral rotator, pushes synthetic snapshots, and validates that minireplay reproduces a failing rule and returns the expected checklist hints. Compatibility: Rotator is opt-in and serves only compact bundles; it does not change the canonical snapshot export schema so long-term archives remain unaffected. The endpoint requires an internal service token and is behind service ACLs by default. Migration notes: Add a small config section to the slo-toolkit helm chart (rotator.enabled, rotator.max_bundles, rotator.byte_budget, rotator.ttl_seconds). If disabled, behavior is identical to current releases. See README additions for examples and runbook snippets. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of rotator and reader - [x] minireplay CLI and help text - [x] Unit tests for rotator concurrency and TTL - [x] Integration test (CI) - [x] Telemetry and dashboards stubbed - [x] Docs and helm values updated Commits summary: "initial rotator impl and interfaces", "add minireplay CLI with fetch/local modes", "add metrics and integ test harness", "trim bundle payloads before publish", "fix race on rotator Close and add graceful shutdown", "address test flakiness and tweak timeouts". Changed files (high-level): slo-toolkit/pkg/snapshot/rotator.go (implements ring buffer, TTL eviction), slo-toolkit/pkg/snapshot/reader.go (compact bundle builder), slo-toolkit/cmd/minireplay/main.go (CLI entrypoint, args, replay runner), slo-toolkit/internal/telemetry/metrics.go (new counters/histograms), slo-toolkit/README.md (docs + examples), slo-toolkit/tests/minireplay_integ_test.go (CI integration test). CI and checks: First CI run failed on flaky integ test (timeout when waiting for ephemeral bundle). I increased test timeouts and added deterministic synthetic clock in test harness. Re-run CI succeeded: build passed, unit tests passed, integration test passed, lint passed. Review conversation highlights: Reviewer Aisha Patel: "Nice incremental API. Two asks: make the rotator evictions opt-in per-namespace and add a stronger assertion around bundle size to avoid OOMs in pathological workloads." Author reply: "PTAL: made evictions namespaced via RotatorConfig.NamespacePolicy and added a hard cap with defensive checks; rotator will reject bundles larger than configured byte_budget and return 413-equivalent error for callers." Reviewer Ben Lang: "Can minireplay replay against an offline trace file? It would help in air-gapped scenarios." Author reply: "Yes, added local bundle mode and README example; flag --local-bundle accepts a path or stdin." Reviewer Marcos Ribeiro: "Telemetry labels look good. Add a boolean flag to opt out from publishing metrics in extremely cost-sensitive tenants." Author reply: "Added RotatorConfig.PublishMetrics bool and tests to assert metric emission toggles." Requested changes and resolution: - Make rotator eviction configurable per-namespace (done). - Add hard bundle size cap and clear error path (done). - Add local-bundle replay mode and docs (done). - Add opt-out for metric emission (done). All reviewers approved after changes. Merge notes: Squash merge after rebase onto main to keep history tidy. Merge method: squash. Post-merge actions: - Add helm values to our infra repo (patch PR queued: INFRA-rotator-values) - Create dashboard tile in observability pack to show rotator churn and replay success (work item: ENG-1848) - Document runbook snippet in the incident-bot playbooks repo to use minireplay for quick repro. Rollout guidance: Start with rotator.enabled=false in production. Enable in staging and two oncall teams for a 2-week trial. Monitor rotator.bundle_rejects and replay.fail_rate; set alert if bundle_rejects > 0.5% or replay.fail_rate increases by >10% from baseline. Security notes: API requires internal service token and enforces the same RBAC rules as snapshot export endpoints; minireplay local mode has no network access unless --sandbox is set. Performance: The rotator is memory-bounded by rotator.byte_budget per-namespace; we use pre-allocated buffer slices and zero-copy io for bundle transfer to reduce GC pressure. Tests and QA: Unit tests cover concurrency and TTL eviction; integration test runs with synthetic telemetry and validates replay produces expected checklist items. Observability: Added counters: rotator.published, rotator.evicted, rotator.rejected_size, replay.success, replay.failure. Dashboards: sample Grafana tile added to docs. Known limitations: The compact bundle trims some context to keep size small, which can occasionally cause non-deterministic replays for very pathological race conditions; we document this limitation and recommend full snapshot export when deeper forensic work is required. Why this is different from previous work: Many earlier PRs focused on large snapshot exports and long-term retention; this PR targets ephemeral, rotating, smallest-viable snapshots and a low-friction CLI to enable faster oncall repros without burdening long-term storage.
